name: OH-12
label: Likely R

key_factors: Balderson's ~$2.0 million cash advantage vs. Christian's $19,000
No public polling or expert ratings; low-profile challenger campaign
model.rationale: An R+15 seat with a well-funded incumbent leaves little room for an upset: Balderson holds a roughly 100-to-1 cash advantage, markets price him near 94%, and Christian's $84,000 in fundraising signals a low-budget campaign. Every available signal points to a comfortable Republican hold.
model.watch: A late surge of Democratic outside spending or a national environment far more favorable to Democrats than currently expected could narrow the margin, though an upset would require more than either alone.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Ohio's 12th District sits firmly in Republican territory, with a partisan lean of roughly fifteen points toward the GOP. Troy Balderson has held the seat since 2018 and returns this cycle with a commanding financial position: nearly $2 million on hand after raising $1.7 million, against about $19,000 for Democrat Jerrad Christian, who has raised under $85,000. No outside spending has materialized on either side, and prediction markets give Balderson roughly a 94% chance of winning.

With no public polls or expert ratings covering the district, the picture rests on district fundamentals and market pricing. Those signals align: the seat's lean, the incumbent's money edge, and the challenger's low profile all point to a comfortable Republican hold. Christian would need a dramatic shift in the national environment or a late influx of outside support to make this competitive, and nothing in the current evidence suggests one is underway.
